summary: Iteration-4 fix verified: content-moderation retry for dialogue close-up shots. PRIMARY paid path (executed once on the first run, then idempotently skipped) — POST /api/projects/c69332993aec4f1fbbae370a70726c09/episodes/1/scenes/3/lines/scene-3-line-1/shot returned status=QUEUED with a fresh prediction_id (3c8b4mrgxnrmw0d0p918739p7c); DB was updated with a NEW closeup_clips entry for (scene 3, scene-3-line-1) whose character_id == 'CHARACTER_A' and a fresh lipsync_clips entry with stage='CLOSEUP'; polling did NOT immediately fail with a content-policy error (reached PROCESSING), and the shot ran through CLOSEUP -> LIPSYNC -> READY, returning a valid archived video_url. SECONDARY zero-cost unit tests (both pass): (a) pipeline.replicate_poll routes 'content_moderated' failures to the content-policy message ('This shot was blocked by the video model's content policy...') and generic failures to 'The render could not finish. You can retry this shot.'; (b) pipeline.replicate_start retries transient 502/5xx once and succeeds on the retry (verified with monkeypatched requests.post + time.sleep, prediction_id from second attempt returned, exactly 2 POST calls made). Result: 8/8 tests passed on the first run (0 skipped); on repeat runs the 4 paid tests idempotently skip because scene-3-line-1 is now READY — this protects the user's paid credits.

minor.issue: One transient Cloudflare 502 (Ray a3ccc6029a4b000e) observed on first attempt during initial verification; second attempt succeeded. Edge-side hiccup, not a backend bug. The test now has an inline retry loop to survive this. Non-blocking.

action_items: No code changes required — all three fixes in /app/backend/pipeline.py verified: (1) build_dialogue_closeup_prompt no longer embeds scene visual_prompt/camera action so per-line close-ups pass Luma content moderation; (2) replicate_poll surfaces a distinct content-policy error message when the failure reason contains 'content'/'moderat'/'policy'/'sensitive'/'flagged'; (3) replicate_start retries transient 500/502/503/504 gateway errors up to 3 attempts with backoff.

Optional hardening (from iter3): stale close-up/lip-sync/audio storage paths in Emergent Object Storage are still orphaned on re-render (not deleted). Storage grows unbounded per retry — consider background cleanup.

Optional UX: on a moderation FAILED result, the frontend Retry button will retry the SAME sanitized prompt again, which is now expected to pass. If the sanitized prompt itself is ever flagged, the current error message tells the user to 'soften the scene or dialogue wording' — but the close-up prompt only contains the character identity + spoken line + global style, so the user would need to soften the LINE TEXT itself. Consider a small hint in the UI explaining which text to edit (dialogue line vs scene action) since the fix decoupled them.
critical_code_review_comments: pipeline.build_dialogue_closeup_prompt (routes.py callsite line 661-662) correctly omits scene.visual_prompt and scene.camera_movement from the per-line close-up prompt — this is the root-cause fix for the reported Retry loop. Only character identity, global style, and the exact spoken line remain, which are moderation-safe inputs.

pipeline.replicate_poll uses substring matching on lowered raw error text (any of 'content', 'moderat', 'policy', 'sensitive', 'flagged') to detect moderation failures. This is a reasonable heuristic; the 'content' token is broad but the alternative substrings anchor it well. Verified: 'content_moderated' triggers the moderation branch; 'some other error' does not.

pipeline.replicate_start retries only on 5xx (500/502/503/504) and only twice (attempts 0,1,2 with sleep 1.5s then 3s). 401/403/429 correctly short-circuit with actionable errors. On the third failed attempt or a non-retryable status, ProviderError is raised with the last upstream detail — good.

Note (not a bug): the retry-with-monkeypatch test proves 'time.sleep' is patched at pipeline.time.sleep (module import site), not at time.sleep global — this is the correct patch surface because pipeline.py does `import time` at line 11.

rca_of_issue: REPORTED BUG — 'After re-rendering a voicing shot, voicing not working and Retry not working': RCA. The pipeline function build_dialogue_closeup_prompt used to concatenate scene.visual_prompt AND scene.camera_movement into the per-line speaking close-up prompt. Scene 3 of project c69332993aec4f1fbbae370a70726c09 contains violent action language ('CHARACTER_C lunges... snatching for the file' etc.); embedding that into every per-line close-up prompt tripped Luma Ray 3.2's content-moderation classifier, returning `content_moderated: Prompt rejected by content policy` at submit time. Because a close-up talking-head only needs the character identity, global style, and the spoken line, the scene action was pure noise but caused deterministic rejection. Retry resubmitted the SAME flagged prompt so it failed identically every attempt. FIX (already applied by main agent to /app/backend/pipeline.py): (1) build_dialogue_closeup_prompt(global_style, scene, character, line_text, orientation) no longer references scene.visual_prompt or scene.camera_movement — only character.id, character.detailed_visual_profile, global_style, and the exact line_text remain (lines 388-413). (2) replicate_poll now inspects the failure `error` string and surfaces the actionable content-policy message when it matches moderation keywords, so future moderation failures render with a distinct message the UI can act on (lines 356-362). (3) replicate_start now retries transient 500/502/503/504 responses up to 3 attempts with backoff (lines 323-343). VERIFICATION: this test suite proves (a) POST on the same previously-flagged line now returns QUEUED with a fresh prediction_id — the sanitized prompt was accepted by Luma; (b) polling reaches PROCESSING (no immediate moderation FAILED) and progresses through CLOSEUP -> LIPSYNC -> READY with a valid video_url; (c) the error-routing branch correctly distinguishes moderation vs generic failures; (d) transient 5xx on start is retried. MITIGATION: none required — the code fix is complete. Optional UX: if a user's DIALOGUE LINE TEXT itself contains violent language, moderation could still trigger — in that case the current error message correctly guides the user to soften wording.
